directions.label: Adaptive Asymmetric
directions.signature: one offset primary object or task with a visible counterweight and a deliberate next-step reveal

firstViewport.layout: asymmetric two-region composition; dominant object/work surface gets 55-65% of the visual weight and the supporting rail gets the rest
firstViewport.alignmentAxis: one strong left or right edge; title, object, and action share an axis instead of floating in a centered stack
firstViewport.dominant: the real object, content, or task supplied by the brief
firstViewport.counterweight: short specific title, one action, and one proof/state cue
firstViewport.belowFoldPeek: one next proof relationship enters the viewport; never a row of identical cards

layoutRules: Choose an intentional offset before choosing a color palette.
Keep one dominant region and one counterweight; do not split attention across equal panels.
Use a list, rail, strip, or open canvas before inventing a card for every section.
Reserve the first viewport for object, meaning, and action; move secondary explanation below.

typeRules.roles: one UI/body family with eyebrow, title, body, label, and action roles; add a display face only after real content earns it
typeRules.title: desktop 48-64px, mobile 34-42px, 1-3 lines, no all-caps paragraph headlines
typeRules.hierarchy: three dominant text levels maximum in the first viewport; metadata stays visibly subordinate
typeRules.tracking: default tracking first; never tighten text to rescue a weak width decision

spacingRules.section: 64-120px vertical sections, adjusted by content proof rather than empty theater
spacingRules.alignment: repeat one axis across title, object, caption, and action; break it once deliberately

surfaceRules.cardBudget: 0-2 framed cards per viewport; repeated content uses rows, open sections, or a single frame
surfaceRules.radius: one primary radius family, usually 0-16px; pills only for compact status or navigation
surfaceRules.elevation: one surface lift plus one active/focus treatment; no shadow ladder
surfaceRules.contrast: separate canvas, object, and action by tone before adding effects

contentRules: Replace abstract value claims with one object, fact, constraint, or outcome.
Do not invent a product category, workflow, or commerce path when the request did not supply one.
A missing asset is a direction decision: generate/find a real one or design a complete assetless surface.
antiAiChecks: No centered-everything hero.
No default three-column card grid.
No interchangeable 'beautiful, powerful, seamless' copy.
No gradient, glass, glow, or oversized type used as the point of view.
No more than two competing accents in the first viewport.
renderChecks: The first read is identifiable in a grayscale screenshot.
The title does not wrap into an accidental orphan line on mobile.
The next section is visibly related to the primary object, not generic filler.
The page still has a recognizable silhouette with color and motion removed.

directions.label: Object-Led Editorial
directions.signature: the product or work object carries the visual identity while copy and proof arrive in measured chapters

firstViewport.layout: large object field with an offset title/action rail; use the next chapter as a visible edge or caption, not a hero-only void
firstViewport.alignmentAxis: object axis and copy axis are related but not mechanically centered
firstViewport.dominant: real product, work, or authored media with visible material/detail
firstViewport.counterweight: short claim, context label, and one inspect/continue action
firstViewport.belowFoldPeek: first feature/material/work proof with a different crop or scale

layoutRules: Show the object before explaining it, but keep the action and practical path visible.
Use one promise per chapter; do not repeat the same split hero pattern down the page.
Alternate scale or alignment to create rhythm; keep the object identity continuous.
Use comparison or purchase details after understanding, not as the opening grid.

typeRules.roles: quiet UI/body face plus one earned display role for product names or chapter claims
typeRules.title: desktop 56-88px only for short, specific claims; mobile 36-52px with explicit line breaks
typeRules.body: 42-66ch, 16-18px, generous line-height; specs use compact utility type
typeRules.hierarchy: one display claim, one supporting explanation, one factual caption; do not create five headline scales
typeRules.tracking: neutral or slightly open display tracking; never use negative tracking as a luxury shortcut

spacingRules.container: 1180-1440px when media needs room; preserve readable copy measure inside it
spacingRules.section: 96-160px when a new object/proof relationship starts; tighter around specs and decisions
spacingRules.alignment: one asymmetry per chapter; do not repeat identical 50/50 splits

surfaceRules.cardBudget: cards only for discrete variants, specs, or work items; never for every feature chapter
surfaceRules.radius: object frames may be square or restrained; controls share one smaller radius
surfaceRules.elevation: material comes from crop, tone, edge, and object detail; avoid floating-card theater
surfaceRules.contrast: let product finish or image treatment carry identity; keep chrome quiet

contentRules: Every visual claim needs an object, material, performance, or use-context proof.
Use real product facts and specific verbs; do not write generic premium language.
Show compatibility, variants, specs, or next action before a decorative social-proof band.
antiAiChecks: No fake product render or atmosphere-only hero.
No repeated 50/50 image-text blocks.
No generic luxury palette without material evidence.
No purchase/spec path hidden behind scroll choreography.
No stock image used as product proof.
renderChecks: Object silhouette and focal crop remain legible on desktop and mobile.
At least three chapters have different composition or scale, not just different copy.
Practical information survives with motion and color disabled.
The first viewport shows the object, claim, and next proof relationship together.

directions.label: Rail And Canvas Workbench
directions.signature: a primary work object stays visually dominant while navigation and inspection controls form a quiet rail

firstViewport.layout: rail + primary canvas/work surface + optional inspector; use one clear work object rather than a dashboard header and tile wall
firstViewport.alignmentAxis: work object owns the main axis; controls align to its edges and state changes stay local
firstViewport.dominant: active canvas, selected record, document, or media object
firstViewport.counterweight: compact navigation, inspector, or command affordance
firstViewport.belowFoldPeek: the next object state, detail group, or history/feedback path

layoutRules: Put the work object above decorative or explanatory chrome.
Use rows, sections, and rails for repeated controls; reserve cards for actual objects.
Make selection, preview, and inspector move as one object through transitions.
On mobile, collapse the rail into an explicit sheet/tab path instead of shrinking desktop chrome.

typeRules.roles: one readable UI face; mono only for code, IDs, shortcuts, or machine state
typeRules.title: 24-40px desktop, 22-32px mobile; compact enough to leave room for work
typeRules.body: 45-75ch for help/copy; 13-16px for controls according to density
typeRules.hierarchy: selected object > active action > context > navigation; do not use display type in chrome
typeRules.tracking: normal tracking; use weight and spacing rather than condensed uppercase labels

spacingRules.container: full available viewport with explicit rail, canvas, and inspector minimums
spacingRules.section: 24-64px between work groups; avoid marketing-scale voids
spacingRules.alignment: controls align to work-object bounds; preserve stable rows during updates

surfaceRules.cardBudget: 0-3 cards; prefer pane, row, strip, table, and canvas primitives
surfaceRules.radius: 4-12px for controls and panes; no pill-shaped buttons unless the action is compact status/navigation
surfaceRules.elevation: use dividers and surface contrast before shadows
surfaceRules.contrast: focus and selection must be obvious without relying on color alone

contentRules: Name the active object and next action in the first read.
Keep labels concrete and short; expose recovery, dirty, saved, and error states.
Do not turn a work surface into a marketing hero.
antiAiChecks: No hero heading above the work object.
No KPI tile row unless metrics are the actual work object.
No rounded-card wrapper around every panel.
No hover-only command discovery.
No dark mode chosen solely to look technical.
renderChecks: The active work object is visible before navigation explanation.
Rail, canvas, and inspector remain distinguishable in grayscale.
Mobile has a deliberate list/sheet order, not accidental wrapping.
A non-default state can be understood without animation.

directions.label: Data And Detail Workbench
directions.signature: comparison, detail, and context remain visible while the data changes

firstViewport.layout: compact filter/context bar above a dominant table or chart-detail relationship; avoid a headline and KPI tile preamble
firstViewport.alignmentAxis: columns, numbers, headers, and selected detail share a strict grid
firstViewport.dominant: table, chart, map, or live status object
firstViewport.belowFoldPeek: one deeper row/detail state or comparison path

layoutRules: Show the data relationship before decorative summary cards.
Preserve row/object identity during filter, sort, and selection changes.
Use semantic color sparingly and pair it with labels, position, or shape.
Put definitions, freshness, units, and partial/error state close to the data.

typeRules.roles: one UI face with tabular-number support; no display role for dashboard chrome
typeRules.title: 24-36px desktop, 22-30px mobile; title must not push the data below the fold
typeRules.body: 14-16px for dense surfaces, 45-80ch for explanation, 12-13px only for metadata
typeRules.hierarchy: data object > selected context > controls > explanatory metadata
typeRules.tracking: normal tracking; align numeric columns mechanically and optically

spacingRules.container: full-width work area with readable detail measure; avoid excessive max-width around tables
spacingRules.section: 24-56px between data relationships; no empty hero band
spacingRules.alignment: headers, values, units, and selected detail share predictable columns

surfaceRules.cardBudget: 0-2 summary cards; table/chart/detail should be open work surfaces
surfaceRules.radius: 4-10px for controls and panels; avoid pill metrics
surfaceRules.elevation: dividers, selected row treatment, and tonal surfaces before shadows
surfaceRules.contrast: states must remain legible in grayscale and at reduced contrast

contentRules: Every metric needs unit, time context, freshness, or comparison context.
Name empty, partial, stale, permission, and error states before styling the chart.
Do not use a colorful chart to compensate for a missing analytical relationship.
antiAiChecks: No four-KPI hero row by default.
No rainbow chart palette without a data model.
No chart detached from table/detail context.
No tiny gray labels as the only explanation.
No animated data changes without a real event.
renderChecks: The data object and current context are readable at first glance.
Long labels, numbers, units, and mixed language do not collide.
Selection/filtering preserves identity and scroll context.
Partial and empty states retain the same hierarchy as the ready state.

directions.label: Stateful Instrument
directions.signature: process state is the product object; the interface makes waiting, change, and recovery legible

firstViewport.layout: one live state surface with a compact context rail and visible next action; no generic hero before the process object
firstViewport.alignmentAxis: state marker, current object, content stream, and action share a timeline or row axis
firstViewport.dominant: conversation, playback object, task trace, waveform, or live process
firstViewport.counterweight: status context, controls, and recovery action
firstViewport.belowFoldPeek: next state specimen, history, or implementation proof

layoutRules: Treat loading/thinking/streaming/approval/error as designed states, not skeleton decoration.
Keep the object anchored while content or status changes.
Make cancel, retry, pause, permission, and final state visible.
Use a stable rail or timeline instead of stacking conversational cards by default.

typeRules.roles: compact UI sans with optional mono for traces, IDs, or machine output; display type only for a short product/state claim
typeRules.title: 28-48px for the main object/state; 22-34px mobile; never let a decorative title hide process context
typeRules.body: 14-17px with clear state labels; stream content gets readable 45-72ch measure
typeRules.hierarchy: current state > content/result > next action > trace metadata
typeRules.tracking: normal tracking; distinguish states through labels and structure, not letter spacing

spacingRules.container: 900-1240px depending on stream/detail split; protect reading measure
spacingRules.section: 32-72px between state specimens; tighter within a live trace
spacingRules.alignment: state markers and content rows share a stable origin

surfaceRules.cardBudget: use contained surfaces for decisions or discrete states; avoid a stack of identical chat cards
surfaceRules.radius: 6-14px; avoid excessive pill badges and floating glass
surfaceRules.elevation: status contrast and border rhythm before glow
surfaceRules.contrast: state text and icon/shape cues must survive reduced motion and color loss

contentRules: Never imply intelligence with an always-loading placeholder.
Show what changed, what is waiting, and what the user can do next.
Use deterministic mock state only when the backend is unavailable, and label it honestly.
antiAiChecks: No generic AI gradient orb or glowing chat shell.
No endless typing indicator as the main state model.
No status communicated only through color or animation.
No assistant persona copy without a concrete workflow.
No card stack that hides the current task.
renderChecks: A user can explain the current state without motion.
Streaming, waiting, success, and error differ structurally, not only chromatically.
The primary action and recovery path remain visible at mobile width.
Interrupted or reduced-motion states retain the same information hierarchy.

directions.label: Specimen Catalog
directions.signature: the working specimen is the content; browsing structure stays quiet and the examples keep stable geometry

firstViewport.layout: compact index plus one strong specimen and a visible next example; use a gallery grid only when comparison is the job
firstViewport.alignmentAxis: index, specimen title, preview frame, and install/action affordance share a consistent axis
firstViewport.dominant: real interactive component or target workflow specimen
firstViewport.counterweight: category/index and concise implementation entry point
firstViewport.belowFoldPeek: one contrasting specimen with the same frame grammar

layoutRules: Show the component working before explaining it.
Keep preview frame dimensions stable; let the inner specimen carry variation.
Use one strong visual language across examples without flattening their content.
Keep copy short and implementation entry points near the working object.

typeRules.roles: bold but controlled specimen title plus compact neutral metadata and action labels
typeRules.title: 40-72px for the catalog thesis; 24-40px for specimen titles; mobile steps down explicitly
typeRules.body: 14-17px, short and concrete; code/props use restrained mono
typeRules.hierarchy: specimen > action > implementation metadata; never let a marketing title dominate the demo
typeRules.tracking: use default or slightly open display tracking; avoid dense uppercase labels

spacingRules.section: 72-120px between specimen groups; captions stay close to their object
spacingRules.alignment: preview geometry is consistent; text can vary without moving the frame

surfaceRules.cardBudget: preview frames are allowed; decorative cards around them are not
surfaceRules.radius: one frame radius plus one control radius; avoid pill overload
surfaceRules.elevation: contained preview contrast, not page-wide glass or glow
surfaceRules.contrast: the specimen must remain legible with the page effects removed

contentRules: Use realistic states and target-specific labels; never copy demo copy blindly.
Each specimen needs a trigger, response, final state, and fallback.
A catalog is not a substitute for a usable product workflow.
antiAiChecks: No unrelated effect collage.
No identical demo cards with different headings only.
No dark-glow skin inherited from a component source by default.
No pointer-only specimen without keyboard/touch behavior.
No hero copy before the first working specimen.
renderChecks: The specimen is legible before its caption is read.
Frames do not jump when states change.
The index and install/action path remain usable on mobile.
At least one specimen shows a non-default state.

directions.label: Narrative Chapters
directions.signature: a controlled sequence of claims, proof, and breathing space; every chapter changes the reading relationship

firstViewport.layout: one strong claim paired with real proof media and a visible continuation cue; avoid an empty centered hero
firstViewport.alignmentAxis: a clear editorial edge or baseline carries title, caption, and media
firstViewport.dominant: real product, work, person, place, or authored media
firstViewport.counterweight: specific claim, caption, and one action
firstViewport.belowFoldPeek: the next proof chapter with a changed crop, scale, or alignment

layoutRules: Each chapter must add a new proof relationship, not just a new background.
Alternate composition, crop, scale, or alignment to avoid a repeated split template.
Keep the next section visible enough to create rhythm without hiding the current action.
Use display type sparingly and only where the media can carry the claim.

typeRules.roles: body/UI face plus one editorial display role; captions and navigation remain compact
typeRules.title: 52-96px for short earned claims; mobile 36-56px with explicit line breaks and no orphan words
typeRules.body: 42-68ch, 16-19px, strong line-height; captions 12-14px with adequate contrast
typeRules.hierarchy: one claim, one proof, one caption; avoid six competing headline treatments
typeRules.tracking: display tracking is neutral or open; never compress to manufacture drama

spacingRules.section: 112-180px only when a new proof chapter earns the space
spacingRules.alignment: repeat one editorial edge, then break it once for emphasis

surfaceRules.cardBudget: 0-3 cards; use image fields, rules, captions, and open bands instead
surfaceRules.radius: use media-specific framing; do not round every section
surfaceRules.elevation: image crop and tonal separation before overlays or blur
surfaceRules.contrast: copy must remain readable over media without a permanent dark veil

contentRules: A headline must name a thing, action, material, or outcome, not only an adjective.
Real media appears early and has a recorded source/generation path.
Keep proof, constraints, and next action visible; atmosphere is supplementary.
antiAiChecks: No giant headline over an empty gradient.
No repeated image-left/text-right sections.
No generic inspirational copy.
No dark overlay hiding weak or low-quality media.
No scroll choreography that removes normal document access.
renderChecks: The first viewport communicates what the thing is before the slogan is interpreted.
Every chapter has a distinct visual reason to exist.
Text remains readable and intentional at mobile width.
The page still works as a static sequence with motion removed.

directions.label: Spatial Inspection
directions.signature: camera, object state, and supporting information explain one inspectable spatial relationship

firstViewport.layout: unframed or lightly framed object stage with compact controls and a clear poster/loading state
firstViewport.alignmentAxis: object framing and control cluster share a predictable origin
firstViewport.belowFoldPeek: a detail, configuration, or static proof path

layoutRules: Frame the object before adding camera or effect complexity.
Keep controls close to the relationship they change.
Use bounded interaction and a normal-flow fallback; never make the canvas the only information path.
Show the object in a meaningful state, not an aimless rotation.

typeRules.roles: stable UI face plus restrained technical labels for object/state values
typeRules.title: 28-56px for the object claim; controls stay compact and readable
typeRules.body: 14-17px, concise metadata, explicit units and state labels
typeRules.tracking: normal tracking; do not use futuristic letter spacing as a substitute for object quality

spacingRules.container: full-width stage with bounded content/control regions
spacingRules.alignment: camera, object, and control bounds remain stable through state changes

surfaceRules.cardBudget: 0-2 control surfaces; the object stage is not a card stack
surfaceRules.radius: frame and controls use restrained, consistent geometry
surfaceRules.elevation: lighting, object material, and stage contrast before decorative glow
surfaceRules.contrast: poster, loading, error, and ready states are all legible

contentRules: Name what the user can inspect or configure and what changes as a result.
Provide object media, poster, loading, error, and low-power fallback evidence.
Technical claims need visible object or specification support.
antiAiChecks: No generic rotating object with no task.
No unbounded canvas or effect-only hero.
No controls hidden inside the scene.
No spatial effect without a static and reduced-motion path.
No invented object media presented as real product evidence.
renderChecks: Object scale and camera framing are intentional at desktop and mobile sizes.
The first frame is useful before interaction begins.
Controls remain reachable and understandable without hover.
The static fallback preserves the object and decision path.
